purpose: Estimate mechanical-harvest windows per Shoreline Fruit growing region. Field color, firmness, and processor specs override the model.

dafb.name: Days after full bloom
dafb.source: MSU Extension / industry: tart cherries typically 60–70 days blossom to harvest; USDA RMA usual Michigan dates imply ~60–75 DAFB by region

gdd_after_bloom.name: GDD base 4°C after full bloom (Zavalloni heat units)
gdd_after_bloom.source: Zavalloni et al. 2006 use GDD base 4°C for Montmorency fruit growth. Peak ~950 after bloom ≈ 65 days at typical June–July orchard temperatures. Labeled as a heat-unit analog, not the unpublished double-sigmoid coefficients.

gdd42_from_mar1.name: MSU-style GDD base 42°F from 1 March
gdd42_from_mar1.source: NWMHRC 2020 growth-stage sheet: tart fruit harvested near 2040 GDD42 (from Mar 1). Bloom that year was ~370 GDD42.

swd.source: MSU NW Hort: SWD did not infest at ~530 GDD base 4°C (green fruit). Color change is the field trigger (Rothwell / Good Fruit Grower).

usda_rma_usual.source: USDA RMA tart cherry feasibility handbook, usual bloom and harvesting dates

nwmhrc_mean_bloom.source: NWMHRC Traverse City full-bloom dates, Montmorency, long-term mean ~May 10–13 (1983–2021 sheet)

ops.note: Mechanical harvest runs day and night; hydro-cool target 35°F. Dry fruit and moderate temperatures protect color and firmness for the processor.

satellite.note: PlanetScope red/green index is a coarse canopy-scale color proxy, not fruit-level Brix. Use only as supporting evidence when summer scenes exist.
